summary: A multi-type live search degrades without lying: results already collected survive a later non-rejection error, only a 400 counts as a per-type market rejection, the live-type whitelist gates only requests that reach the API, and an incomplete result set says so in meta.reason rather than only on stderr.
reason: Fanning a search across every catalog type creates four ways to be wrong that a single-type search does not have, and each one fails silently. Returning on a mid-loop 5xx discards hits already gathered and skips the network-error check that owns the local fallback. Treating any 4xx as "this type is unavailable" replays an auth or rate-limit failure across seven requests and reports it as market unavailability. Validating the type before the data-source branch lets a live-API whitelist reject resource types the local index legitimately holds. And a degraded envelope that is shape-identical to a complete one leaves a stdout-only consumer no way to know results are missing. A regeneration that reintroduces the fan-out must carry all four properties, not just the happy path.
validated_outcome: Six tests pin the contract: earlier hits survive a 500 on a later candidate; 429/401/403/404 propagate without fan-out; --type browse --data-source local exits 0 again (it exited 2 before); meta.reason names the excluded type in both plain-JSON and --agent envelopes; and a complete search carries no reason. verify_skill, go build, go vet, go test ./..., and govulncheck all pass.
